Theme

School & learning

parse verb

also parsing, parse a word, parse a sentence, analyse a sentence

classical

Quint. 1.8.13: ut partēs ōrātiōnis reddī sibi solūtō versū dēsīderet

partēs ōrātiōnis reddere

to parse, to say what part of speech each word is

Quintilian’s grammarian, reading a poem with his pupils, has them break up the verse and give back the parts of speech. Literally “to render the parts of speech”.

Other words

  • proprietātēs dēscrībere — to parse, to describe the properties of a word

    with the genitive of the word: proprietātēs nōminis, verbī · also used · modern · Traupman 223, 238, 248

    Traupman’s phrase: Dēscrībe proprietātēs «magister» nōminis, parse the noun “magister” (223). Classically proprietās verbōrum is the proper sense of words (Quintilian, Lewis & Short); we have not found the phrase for parsing.

Examples

  • in praelegendō grammaticus et illa quidem minōra praestāre dēbēbit, ut partēs ōrātiōnis reddī sibi solūtō versū dēsīderet et pedum proprietātēs

    in reading aloud first, the grammarian must also see to smaller things: when the verse has been broken up, he should require the parts of speech to be given back to him, and the qualities of the feetQuint. 1.8.13

  • Dēscrībāmus nunc proprietātēs dictiōnum in hāc sententiā.

    Let us now parse the words of this sentence.Traupman 238

See also part of speech, grammar, sentence.

SourcesLewis & Short: pars · Lewis & Short: oratio · Lewis & Short: reddo · Lewis & Short: proprietas · Lewis & Short: describo
